gridflow explorer is a web app for browsing gridflow’s data: GB and European energy-market data from eight public sources, and the tables gridflow builds from them. A React and TypeScript front end sits on a FastAPI backend that reads gridflow through its own client.

The rest of gridflow
React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Recharts and React Router.
No component kit and no CSS framework: its own design tokens as CSS custom properties, light and dark themes, and one shared chart theme.
One dataset page template with three bodies: series as a chart, event feeds as a filterable table, reference tables as a plain table.
Its own screenshot tool, headless Chrome through puppeteer-core, takes every screen in light and dark.
Python, FastAPI on uvicorn, Polars, and DuckDB opened read-only per request.
It reads gridflow only through gridflow’s own client, GridflowClient, never raw file paths.
Endpoints serve the source manifest, a dataset’s rows and its coverage, forecast runs from the gold forecast store, and a job that runs gridflow’s ingestion to fill a missing range.
How it’s built
A view is a small typed file
Each dataset view is its own folder, src/views/<source>/<family>/, and the app finds views by a file glob: adding a view is adding a folder, with no central list to edit.
